exercise1.prompt: coordinates = (10, 20), print the x and the y

hiddenCases.name: coordinates is a tuple, so nothing can be appended to it
hiddenCases.describe: a tuple has no append(), which is what makes it immutable

exercise1.hint: Parentheses are what make a tuple; square brackets would give you a list that looks almost the same and behaves differently. Reading from it works exactly as it does for a list.

questions.prompt: What happens when you run point = (1, 2) and then point[0] = 5?
choices: A TypeError, because a tuple cannot be changed
questions.explain: A tuple supports item assignment nowhere, so Python refuses rather than quietly making a copy. Build a new tuple if you need different values.

questions.prompt: Which of these are true of a tuple?
choices: Its items stay in the order you wrote them
You can add items with append()
You can read items with an index
A for loop can walk it
questions.explain: Everything that only reads a tuple works. append() is the one that does not exist, because growing it would be a change.

questions.prompt: For coordinates = (10, 20), the y-coordinate is coordinates[___].
questions.explain: Tuples are indexed from 0 exactly as lists are, so the second value sits at index 1.

questions.prompt: Why would you choose a tuple over a list?
choices: It is always faster to write
Because the data should not change, and a tuple makes an accidental change impossible
Because tuples can hold more items
questions.explain: The immutability is the point. Days of the week or a fixed coordinate should not be editable, and a tuple says so in the code itself.
